reasoning.title: Union querysets with order_by require careful column tracking in SQL compilation
reasoning.description: WHEN: A QuerySet uses `.union()` or other combinators (`.intersection()`, `.difference()`) with `.order_by()`, especially when followed by `.values_list()` or `.values()` that changes the select list.
reasoning.content: The SQL compiler's `get_order_by()` method in `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py` must handle combinator queries where ORDER BY columns may not exist in the final select list. When a combinator query has `values_select` defined, order by expressions need to be resolved against the combined query's actual columns, not just the first subquery's columns. The fix requires checking if an order by column exists in the select list before attempting to reference it by position.

reasoning.title: Test combinator queries with derived querysets and column filtering
reasoning.description: WHEN: Writing tests for union/intersection/difference operations in `tests/queries/test_qs_combinators.py`.
reasoning.content: Add test cases that combine: (1) combinator operations with `.order_by()`, (2) followed by `.values_list()` or `.values()` that restrict columns, (3) then re-evaluate the queryset. This reproduces the issue where ORDER BY position references become invalid after the select list changes. Include tests with both explicit column ordering and F-expression ordering.

reasoning.title: Aggregate template spacing with DISTINCT modifier
reasoning.description: WHEN fixing issues where aggregate functions (Count, Sum, etc.) combine DISTINCT with expressions that lack leading whitespace (like CASE WHEN), especially when the template uses `%(distinct)s%(expressions)s` pattern.
reasoning.content: The DISTINCT keyword in SQL aggregate functions requires a trailing space before the expression it modifies. When `extra_context['distinct']` is set to 'DISTINCT' without a trailing space, it concatenates directly with expressions like CASE, producing invalid SQL (e.g., 'COUNT(DISTINCTCASE WHEN...'). Always include the trailing space: `'DISTINCT '` instead of `'DISTINCT'`.

reasoning.title: Test aggregation changes with runtests.py runner
reasoning.description: WHEN modifying aggregate function behavior in django/db/models/aggregates.py or related SQL generation code, to verify changes don't break existing functionality.
reasoning.content: Use `python tests/runtests.py aggregation -v 0` to quickly run the aggregation test suite (65 tests, ~0.1s). This validates that changes to aggregate templates, distinct handling, or expression rendering don't regress existing queries. The test suite includes models (Author, Book, Publisher, Store) already set up for aggregate testing.

reasoning.title: Identify the minimal change set before exploration
reasoning.description: WHEN modifying Django settings defaults or file handling behavior, BEFORE running exploratory commands
reasoning.content: For a setting default change (like FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS), the minimal change set is: (1) global_settings.py to change the default value, (2) storage.py to handle the new default in permission logic, (3) affected tests to update expectations. Identify these files first via targeted grep, then examine only what's necessary to understand the current implementation.

reasoning.title: Use test failures to guide implementation, not exploration
reasoning.description: WHEN a PR requires changing default behavior that affects test assertions
reasoning.content: Run the existing test suite first to see which tests fail with the proposed change, then fix only those tests. This is faster than manually reading test code — let pytest tell you what breaks. For FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS changes, run `tests/file_storage/tests.py::FileStoragePermissionsTests` to see current behavior, then modify global_settings.py and re-run to identify what test assertions need updating.

reasoning.title: Default FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS setting location and value
reasoning.description: WHEN you need to set a default file upload permission mode that applies to all uploaded files via FileSystemStorage. This applies to any issue about inconsistent file permissions after upload.
reasoning.content: The default FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS is defined in django/conf/global_settings.py (line ~307). Change it from `None` to `0o644` to ensure consistent, readable file permissions regardless of whether TemporaryUploadedFile or MemoryUploadedFile is used during upload.

reasoning.title: How FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS flows through the storage system
reasoning.description: WHEN debugging file permission issues or verifying that permission changes take effect. This applies to understanding how settings propagate to actual file operations.
reasoning.content: FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS from global_settings flows to FileSystemStorage.file_permissions_mode property (django/core/files/storage.py), which is then applied via os.chmod() in the _save() method. The setting_changed signal handler clears cached properties when the setting changes, ensuring dynamic updates work correctly.

reasoning.title: Verify implementation against original tests before reverting test changes
reasoning.description: WHEN modifying implementation that changes how a mocked function is called or what side effects occur, and you've temporarily modified tests to make them pass.
reasoning.content: After reverting test modifications, explicitly re-run the original test suite to confirm the implementation still satisfies the original test expectations. If original tests pass only because they mock at the wrong layer (e.g., mocking `subprocess.call` when code now uses `subprocess.run`), the tests are not actually validating the new behavior. Document why the original tests cannot validate the new implementation, or find a way to make the implementation compatible with original test assumptions.

reasoning.title: Identify test-implementation coupling before starting changes
reasoning.description: WHEN the issue requires changing implementation details that are directly tested (subprocess calls, file I/O, environment variables).
reasoning.content: Before modifying code, analyze what the tests actually verify: do they mock at the subprocess level, check file contents, or validate environment variables? If the new implementation changes the mechanism (e.g., `.pgpass` file → `PGPASSWORD` env var), recognize this requires test updates. Request clarification on whether tests should be updated or implementation should maintain backward-compatible behavior (e.g., support both mechanisms).

reasoning.title: Test mocking strategy must match subprocess API changes
reasoning.description: WHEN refactoring subprocess calls (e.g., from subprocess.check_call to subprocess.run), the test mocks must be updated to match the new function signature and behavior. This applies to any test that patches subprocess functions.
reasoning.content: The failing attempt modified test files despite explicit instructions not to. When changing from subprocess.check_call to subprocess.run, tests that mock subprocess.call must be updated to mock subprocess.run instead, and the mock must handle the new signature (including the env parameter). Verify test expectations match the new implementation before running tests.

reasoning.title: Environment variable approach requires test mock updates for environment inspection
reasoning.description: WHEN switching from temporary file-based credentials (PGPASSFILE) to environment variables (PGPASSWORD), test infrastructure must be updated to inspect the environment dict passed to subprocess.run rather than reading files. This applies to any credential-passing refactor.
reasoning.content: The old tests checked for PGPASSFILE in os.environ and read its contents. With PGPASSWORD, tests must mock subprocess.run to capture the env parameter and verify PGPASSWORD is set correctly in that dict. The test mock signature changes from `_mock_subprocess_call(*args)` to `_mock_subprocess_run(args, env=None, ...)` to properly capture the environment passed to the subprocess.

reasoning.title: Deletion QuerySet optimization requires careful field selection
reasoning.description: WHEN optimizing QuerySets in the deletion collector (django/db/models/deletion.py) to reduce fetched fields, especially in the `related_objects()` method or when collecting related objects for cascade operations.
reasoning.content: Optimizing QuerySets to use `.only()` or `.values()` to fetch fewer fields during deletion requires ensuring that downstream code (CASCADE handlers, add_field_update, etc.) can still access required fields. The objects must remain as model instances (not just values) when passed to `collector.collect()` and `collector.add_field_update()`, since these methods access `objs[0].__class__` and iterate over instances. Test thoroughly with all on_delete handlers (CASCADE, SET_NULL, SET_DEFAULT, PROTECT, DO_NOTHING) to ensure field access doesn't break.

reasoning.title: Deletion tests must cover all on_delete handler types and field access patterns
reasoning.description: WHEN modifying deletion logic in django/db/models/deletion.py, especially when changing how QuerySets are constructed or fields are selected.
reasoning.content: The deletion system has multiple code paths for different on_delete handlers and field types. Run the full test suite in tests/delete/tests.py and verify with multiple database backends (not just SQLite) since some features vary by backend (e.g., `can_defer_constraint_checks`). Pay special attention to tests involving nullable fields, inheritance, and bulk operations, as these exercise different code branches in the collector.
